instagram_carousel.caption:
Costa Rica is on the shortlist. Here is how the legal side works for Australian couples.

There are two routes to the same register: the Registro Civil celebrates civil marriages for foreign applicants, and Costa Rican notaries also celebrate marriages and declare them to the Registro Civil online.

1. Gather your documents. For the Registro Civil, each of you brings a valid passport, plus a birth certificate and a civil status certificate, both apostilled in Australia and officially translated into Spanish. The civil status certificate must be issued no more than one month before you present it, unless it states its own validity, so order it last.
2. Lodge your request together, in person, and both sign it. A notice of your marriage, called an edict, is published in the official gazette, La Gaceta.
3. The ceremony follows on average 4 to 6 months later, depending on the diary. Living in Australia, plan this route around two visits.
4. Name two witnesses. Both attend on the day with a valid identity document and are sworn in during the ceremony.
5. Registration takes 25 working days when either spouse is foreign. Your certificate is then authenticated with an Apostille before it travels home.

Back home, you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place.

Dreaming of vows on a headland lawn or under a rainforest canopy? Ask a notary whether the legal ceremony can take place there. If not, a symbolic ceremony after the legal signing gives you the setting.

newsletter.subject: Getting married in Costa Rica: the legal steps in order
newsletter.preview: Documents, your request, witnesses, registration and your certificate: the sequence for Australian couples.
newsletter.blurb: Costa Rica on your list? Our new guide sets out the legal sequence for Australian couples: apostilled documents translated into Spanish, a request to the Registro Civil or a Costa Rican notary who declares the marriage online, two sworn witnesses, then 25 working days of registration and an Apostille before your certificate travels home. It also covers how your marriage is recognised in Australia, when to marry and the questions to put to any resort.
